title: Title and 1st Point: Discipline and Gratitude Lesson for the Commanding Self

questions.question: What is the main problem the speaker points out in the nafs at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: It loves attention, praise, and feeling important.

questions.question: What two plant examples are used to challenge the nafs’s pride?
questions.answer: A small seed that leads to a fig tree and a dry vine branch that carries many grapes.

questions.question: What idea do those plant examples help explain?
questions.answer: They show that carrying blessings does not mean something created them by its own power.

questions.question: Why is the nafs said to deserve blame instead of admiration?
questions.answer: Because it uses its will badly and harms the value of the blessings given to it.

questions.question: According to the passage, how does pride affect blessings?
questions.answer: It lowers their worth.

questions.question: How does ingratitude affect blessings?
questions.answer: It wipes out their benefit in a moral sense.

questions.question: What is wrong with claiming blessings as one’s own?
questions.answer: It is treated as taking what does not truly belong to the self.

questions.question: What should a person do instead of boasting about good deeds?
questions.answer: Be thankful to Allah.

questions.question: What should replace the desire for fame?
questions.answer: Humility.

questions.question: What should replace the wish for praise?
questions.answer: Repentance and asking Allah for forgiveness.

questions.question: Where does true human perfection lie, according to the passage?
questions.answer: In knowing Allah rather than focusing on oneself.

questions.question: What comparison is made between the nafs in a person and nature in the world?
questions.answer: Both are described as receivers, not real makers.

questions.question: If they are not the true source of good, what role do they have?
questions.answer: They receive what is given and become places where faults and evil are connected.

questions.question: Why were the nafs and nature created as coverings or veils?
questions.answer: So things whose beauty is not obvious would be linked to them, while Allah is known to be free of defect.

questions.question: What mistake do the nafs and nature make after being given that role?
questions.answer: They act as if they are partners with the Creator.

questions.question: How does the passage judge a person who worships the self or nature?
questions.answer: As very foolish and deeply unjust.

questions.question: Why does the passage reject the excuse, “Beauty appears through me, so I must be beautiful”?
questions.answer: Because passing beauty along does not mean the person has made it part of himself.

questions.question: What is the difference between a place of passage and a true possessor in this passage?
questions.answer: A place of passage only carries something through, while a true possessor would really own or contain it.

questions.question: Why does the passage reject the claim, “I was chosen, so I must have special merit”?
questions.answer: Because those gifts were given due to need, weakness, and poverty before Allah, not because of personal greatness.

questions.question: What attitude toward oneself is the reader being taught in this passage?
questions.answer: To be humble, grateful, repentant, and aware of dependence on Allah.

questions.question: What warning from the opening verse matches the lesson of this passage?
questions.answer: People should not feel secure when they enjoy praise for things that are not truly theirs.

questions.question: How is the nafs described in emotional terms near the beginning?
questions.answer: It is drawn to glory, fame, and compliments.

questions.question: What does the passage say would have to be true for the nafs to have a right to boast?
questions.answer: It would have to be the real producer of the blessings it carries.

questions.question: Do the examples in the passage support the idea that the carrier of blessings is their creator?
questions.answer: No, they show that carrying something does not make one its maker.

questions.question: What human ability makes the nafs especially responsible in this passage?
questions.answer: The ability to choose.

questions.question: What is one harmful result of conceit mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: It ruins the blessings morally.

questions.question: What is one harmful result of ungratefulness mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: It cancels out the value of blessings.

questions.question: How does the passage describe taking credit for blessings?
questions.answer: As a wrongful attempt to own what belongs to Allah.

questions.question: Which is the better response to good actions: self-praise or gratitude?
questions.answer: Gratitude.

questions.question: Which is better in this passage: fame or modesty?
questions.answer: Modesty.

questions.question: Which is presented as more fitting than praise from people?
questions.answer: Turning back to Allah in repentance and seeking forgiveness.

questions.question: What does the passage say about being centered on oneself?
questions.answer: It is not the way to reach perfection.

questions.question: What is the proper understanding of the nafs’s role in relation to good?
questions.answer: It receives good but does not produce it independently.

questions.question: What is the proper understanding of its role in relation to evil?
questions.answer: Evil is connected to it because of its failure and misuse.

questions.question: Why does the passage say ugly-looking things may be linked to the nafs and nature?
questions.answer: So Allah’s perfection remains clear and free from blame.

questions.question: What serious spiritual error happens when the nafs forgets its true role?
questions.answer: It behaves as if it shares in the Creator’s work.

questions.question: Why is the statement “I show beauty, so I am beautiful” rejected?
questions.answer: Because showing something is not the same as truly becoming it.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying the person is only a route, not a resting place?
questions.answer: Blessings pass through the person but do not belong to him by his own power.

questions.question: According to the final paragraph, why are gifts given first to such a person?
questions.answer: Because of greater neediness, weakness, and sadness, not because of superiority.

questions.question: What overall lesson should an 8th-grade student take from this passage about success and talents?
questions.answer: They should thank Allah, avoid bragging, and remember that gifts are trusts, not proof of personal greatness.

questions.question: Who is being spoken to directly throughout most of this passage?
questions.answer: The speaker’s own nafs.

questions.question: What tone does the speaker use toward the nafs?
questions.answer: A correcting and humbling tone.

questions.question: What false loves of the nafs are named near the start?
questions.answer: Love of status, fame, and praise.

questions.question: What do the examples of the seed and vine branch have in common?
questions.answer: Both appear small or weak but are linked with many fruits.

questions.question: Why are those examples not meant to prove the nafs is great?
questions.answer: Because they challenge the idea that visible means deserve full credit.

questions.question: What power in the nafs makes its mistakes more blameworthy?
questions.answer: Its free choice.

questions.question: Name two ways the nafs damages blessings according to the passage.
questions.answer: By pride and by ingratitude.

questions.question: What does the passage teach is the right response to blessings from Allah?
questions.answer: Thankfulness.

questions.question: What character quality should take the place of wanting public honor?
questions.answer: Humility.

questions.question: What spiritual action should take the place of wanting compliments?
questions.answer: Repentance and seeking forgiveness.

questions.question: How does the passage define real completion or excellence for a person?
questions.answer: By recognizing Allah instead of being absorbed in the self.

questions.question: In what way are the nafs and nature similar?
questions.answer: Neither is an independent maker; both are receivers.

questions.question: What does the passage say is the only effect truly linked to them?
questions.answer: Becoming the side to which evil is connected.

questions.question: Why is that connection to evil mentioned?
questions.answer: Because they fail to receive and respond properly to the good that comes from absolute goodness.

questions.question: What protective purpose do the veils of nafs and nature serve?
questions.answer: They keep defects from being wrongly attributed to Allah.

questions.question: What happens when they go against that purpose?
questions.answer: They take on a role opposite to what they were created for.

questions.question: What does the passage say about someone who worships himself or nature?
questions.answer: He is acting with foolishness and wrongdoing.

questions.question: Why should a person not think being selected to display good works proves personal worth?
questions.answer: Because the selection can come from greater need, not from greater merit.

questions.question: What three human conditions are mentioned at the end to explain why gifts may be given?
questions.answer: Being spiritually poor, needy, and sorrowful.

questions.question: What is one clear main idea running through the whole passage?
questions.answer: A person should not take Allah’s gifts as proof of his own greatness.

questions.question: What kind of inner struggle is shown in this passage?
questions.answer: A struggle against pride and self-admiration.

questions.question: How does the passage challenge the nafs’s desire to be praised?
questions.answer: It says the nafs does not truly own or produce the blessings for which it wants credit.

questions.question: What role do the examples from plants play in the argument?
questions.answer: They give a simple picture showing that means are not the true source.

questions.question: If the nafs were truly like a real producer, what might it claim?
questions.answer: It might claim a right to boast.

questions.question: Why does the passage say that claim fails in reality?
questions.answer: Because the nafs misuses its will and spoils what it receives.

questions.question: How can a blessing be harmed without disappearing physically?
questions.answer: Its spiritual value can be damaged by arrogance and ingratitude.

questions.question: What duty is given instead of taking pride in good deeds?
questions.answer: Offering thanks to Allah.

questions.question: What attitude is described as suitable for a believer instead of fame?
questions.answer: Humble behavior.

questions.question: What is said to belong to the believer instead of praise?
questions.answer: Repentance and asking for forgiveness.

questions.question: What shows that the passage is not only about behavior but also about belief?
questions.answer: It says true perfection comes from recognizing Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage explain the role of nature and the nafs in relation to actions?
questions.answer: They are not independent doers but receivers and coverings.

questions.question: What does “receiver” suggest in this passage?
questions.answer: That good comes to them, but they do not originate it on their own.

questions.question: Why are they linked with evil?
questions.answer: Because evil appears through their failure, weakness, or misuse.

questions.question: What is the wisdom in having them serve as veils?
questions.answer: It helps people understand that Allah is free from flaw.

questions.question: What does the passage criticize about the way they behave afterward?
questions.answer: They act in a way that competes with the Creator instead of staying in their proper place.

questions.question: Why is saying “beauty shows through me, so I am beautiful” a weak excuse?
questions.answer: Because reflecting something is not the same as possessing it in oneself.

questions.question: What mistaken conclusion about being chosen does the passage correct?
questions.answer: That being used for good works automatically proves personal superiority.

questions.question: According to the passage, what may be the real reason a person receives many gifts?
questions.answer: Greater need and poverty before Allah.

questions.question: How does the final note about neediness deepen the lesson on humility?
questions.answer: It shows gifts may be mercy for the weak, not medals for the great.

questions.question: What should Muslim students learn from this when they do well in school or service?
questions.answer: They should thank Allah, stay humble, and not act as if success came only from themselves.

questions.question: What is the speaker trying to do to the nafs in this passage?
questions.answer: Correct it and bring it down from pride.

questions.question: Which bad habits of the nafs are named first?
questions.answer: Loving honor, fame, praise, and ego.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the example of a tiny beginning leading to many results?
questions.answer: A small means should not act as if it owns all the outcomes.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the branch carrying many clusters?
questions.answer: Holding blessings is not the same as making them.

questions.question: Why is the nafs less excusable than a seed or branch?
questions.answer: Because it has choice and responsibility.

questions.question: What does pride do to the blessings a person receives?
questions.answer: It lowers and harms them spiritually.

questions.question: What does thanklessness do to those blessings?
questions.answer: It removes their value in the sight of proper servanthood.

questions.question: Why is self-claim over blessings described so strongly?
questions.answer: Because the blessings really belong to Allah, not the self.

questions.question: What is the proper reaction to personal achievements according to the passage?
questions.answer: Gratitude, not boasting.

questions.question: What personal quality should a believer seek instead of popularity?
questions.answer: Humility.

questions.question: What should a believer seek instead of compliments?
questions.answer: Forgiveness from Allah.

questions.question: How is human excellence defined here?
questions.answer: By knowing Allah and not making the self the center.

questions.question: What shared role do the nafs and nature have?
questions.answer: They both receive rather than create independently.

questions.question: What side of events are they made to carry?
questions.answer: The side where evil and deficiency are referred.

questions.question: Why is that role important for belief?
questions.answer: It protects Allah’s transcendence and perfection from false blame.

questions.question: What wrong attitude makes them seem like partners to the Creator?
questions.answer: Turning what they receive into a claim of ownership and power.

questions.question: How does the passage evaluate self-worship and nature-worship?
questions.answer: As foolish and unjust.

questions.question: Why does the passage refuse the idea that displaying beauty makes someone beautiful?
questions.answer: Because he only passes it on and does not absorb it into his own essence.

questions.question: What surprising reason is given for why someone may be selected for blessings?
questions.answer: He may be the one most in need of help.

questions.question: How can this passage help a student stay sincere when receiving praise from others?
questions.answer: It reminds him that all good is from Allah and that praise should lead to shukr, not arrogance.

questions.question: What inner enemy is being addressed in the passage?
questions.answer: The commanding self, or nafs.

questions.question: What does that nafs enjoy too much?
questions.answer: Reputation, admiration, and self-importance.

questions.question: What image of fruit-bearing plants is used to test whether pride is justified?
questions.answer: The image of a small source connected to many fruits.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage reach from those images?
questions.answer: The visible means cannot proudly claim to be the true cause of the blessings.

questions.question: Why is the nafs especially responsible for its bad response?
questions.answer: Because it has will and can choose how to respond.

questions.question: What are three wrong things the nafs does with blessings?
questions.answer: It becomes proud, ungrateful, and possessive.

questions.question: What should replace pride in one’s actions?
questions.answer: Thankfulness to Allah.

questions.question: What should replace the search for fame?
questions.answer: Humility.

questions.question: What should replace wanting praise from people?
questions.answer: Repentance and asking Allah to forgive.

questions.question: What is a person’s true perfection said to be?
questions.answer: Recognizing Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage compare the nafs with nature?
questions.answer: It says both have a similar created role as receivers, not independent agents.

questions.question: What does the passage deny about both the nafs and nature?
questions.answer: That they are the real source and doer behind good things.

questions.question: What kind of things are assigned to them through their role as veils?
questions.answer: Things whose outward side seems ugly or defective.

questions.question: What higher belief does this arrangement protect?
questions.answer: That Allah is pure and free from imperfection.

questions.question: What contradiction appears when the nafs forgets this role?
questions.answer: It acts opposite to its created duty and behaves as if it shares lordship.

questions.question: What two forms of false worship are directly criticized?
questions.answer: Worshiping the self and worshiping nature.

questions.question: Why is it not enough to say, “Good appears through me”?
questions.answer: Because being used as a channel does not prove ownership or virtue.

questions.question: What correction is given to the thought, “I was chosen, so I must be special”?
questions.answer: Being chosen may come from need and dependence, not from excellence.

questions.question: What does the ending teach about people who receive many gifts from Allah?
questions.answer: They may be the ones who most need Allah’s mercy and support.

questions.question: What is the best summary of the passage’s message?
questions.answer: Never let blessings make you proud; let them make you thankful, humble, and aware of Allah.
